chunks: Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Ahmad ibn Isa from Ghaylan said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') during the days of Hajj: from which day does it begin and on which day does it end? Is it the same in Mina and all other regions, or is it more in Mina? He said: 'The Takbir in Mina begins after the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Nahr (Eid al-Adha) and continues until the Fajr prayer of the day of departure (Yawm al-Nafar). If he stays for Dhuhr, he says Takbir; if he stays for Asr, he says Takbir; but if he stays for Maghrib, he does not say Takbir. And the Takbir in other regions begins on the Day of Arafah from the Fajr prayer until the first departure (Nafar al-Awwal) and the Dhuhr prayer, and this is the middle of the Days of Tashriq.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report agrees with the general public (Sunni), but we do not act upon it. The action is according to what we have previously mentioned from the reports. The fifth part of the Book of Tahdhib al-Ahkam was completed, and its end is the Book of Hajj, and it is followed in the sixth part by the Book of Visitation (Ziyarat). 'And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.' * And may Allah bless Muhammad and his pure family.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: When does the Takbir begin and end during Hajj according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise temporal boundaries for the ritual Takbir during Hajj, distinguishing between the specific observance in Mina (post-Dhuhr on Eid) and general regions (from Fajr on Arafah until the first departure). Although the narrator notes that this ruling aligns with the Sunni majority, al-Tusi explicitly states that Shia jurisprudence rejects this view in favor of previously established narrations, highlighting a key methodological divergence in ritual timing. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on adhering to the Ahl al-Bayt’s specific instructions over general communal practice during the sacred days of Dhul-Hijjah.
